headline: All majors below the 200-day line; BTC and ETH seeing outflows while whales accumulate spot; funding positive but positioning tilts long and crowded.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguously bearish. Bitcoin trades 49.5% below its 12-month high at 63,053, Ethereum 61% below at 1,881, and every asset in the major seven sits below its 200-day moving average with no golden cross in sight. The 90-day range for Bitcoin spans 58,566 to 77,550; for Ethereum, 1,566 to 2,132. Price action over the last seven days confirms the slouch: Bitcoin down 2.36%, Ethereum down 1.32%, XRP down 5.63%, ADA down 7.84%. The only asset showing a positive 30-day print is Ethereum at 7.07%, a modest rebound that sits within a larger downtrend. Volatility is elevated, with Ethereum and ADA both printing 30-day realized volatility north of 55%, while Bitcoin holds 21.8%. This is the tape of an extended drawdown, not a bounce.

Momentum is mixed and inconsistent, a sign of exhaustion rather than conviction either way. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 43.3, Ethereum at 51.1 (neutral), and XRP at a beaten 35.7. MACD below signal is the dominant picture for Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and ADA, but SOL, BNB, and DOGE print MACD above signal, a minority tell. What matters is the gap between trend and momentum: several assets show RSI near 50 with MACD still below the signal line, which is a quiet divergence, the kind you see when selling pressure eases but the uptrend has not restarted. BNB's RSI at 61.2 stands out as the only overbought reading among the major seven and the only one with MACD above signal; it has gained 5.97% over the last 30 days and 2.35% in seven days. This is not strength in the regime, it is a single asset performing relative to a basket in decline.

Positioning in perpetuals reveals a crowded long bet funded by positive carry. Bitcoin funding prints 0.0053% over eight hours, annualizing to 5.8%, while Ethereum trades at 0.0021% (2.3% annualized). Traders are paying to hold long exposure. The long-short ratio on Bitcoin is 2.21 at OKX, meaning for every short there are 2.21 longs; for Ethereum it is 1.83, for SOL it is 2.4, and for DOGE it reaches 5.51. This is not balanced, and it is not cheap. Open interest across Bitcoin and Ethereum totals 3.48 billion dollars. Liquidations over the past 21 to 24 hours show more shorts being wiped (79,745 dollars in Bitcoin, 263,436 dollars in Ethereum) than longs (56,292 and 129,062 respectively), which can mean either a relief bounce or the tail end of a squeeze; the data does not specify. SOL is the only major showing negative funding at minus 0.0038% per eight hours (minus 4.2% annualized), a tell that shorts are now paying to hold, a potential signal of positioning unwind.

Whale flows over the last 48 hours show 62.6 million dollars in Bitcoin moving onto exchanges at Coinbase, paired with 149.8 million dollars in USDT (Tether) moving onto Bitfinex. This is not accumulation into cold storage; this is deployment toward spot entry. The stablecoin float sits at 306.5 billion, down 0.4% over the last 30 days, a marginal drain but still a large dry powder reserve. The weekly net whale flow over the last four weeks is volatile: positive 445 million, then 1.075 billion outflow, then 67 million in, then minus 507 million out. The most recent swing (the last week captured) shows 507 million net outflow from exchanges, but the 48-hour window cited in the major flows reverses that to inflow. This is choppy, tactical repositioning, not a clear directional commitment.

Sentiment is Fear at 34, down from a 30-day range of 25 to 34, so the gauge is at the weak end of its recent span but not at the extreme low. The tape and the gauge agree that conviction is fading. Total market cap added 0.05% on the day to 2.25 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance holds at 56.2%, meaning large-cap weakness is broad-based. The BTC spot ETF saw 56.2 million in outflows on August 14, the latest dated print, while the last five sessions averaged minus 77 million per day in net outflows; same-direction outflows have persisted for three days. The Ethereum ETF printed positive 5.9 million on August 13, but the five-session net is only plus 9.3 million, a weak bid from traditional finance.

Watch for funding to flip negative across Bitcoin and Ethereum; that would signal shorts are now paying and long leverage is unwinding. Watch for a retest of the 200-day moving average on Bitcoin and Ethereum after a week or two of sideways price action; breakup would be a higher-probability move than the alternative. Watch the whale flow direction over the next five sessions; if the recent inflow onto exchanges reverses back to outflow to cold storage while whales pile in, that is a shift from tactical to accumulative posture and would matter. Until then, the picture is a regime extended lower, positioning crowded and expensive, and flows contradictory.
